patches.summary: Hand-built `records bulk-upsert` wrapper adding --merge-on, --batch-progress, --stdin, and automatic 10-record batching over the generated records upsert path; on mid-run batch failure now emits accumulated results to stderr before returning so callers can see which batches committed.
patches.reason: Airtable caps upserts at 10 records per request, so file/stdin-driven ingest pipelines need a batching wrapper the generator doesn't emit. The wrapper preserves the generated body shape and forwards each batch through the generated client. Greptile P1 review (PR #829) flagged that the original error path discarded accumulated successful results before printing; the partial_results stderr event addresses that without changing the success exit shape.
patches.validated_outcome: Builds, registers under `records` group, forwards each batch through the generated upsert client with stderr progress lines, and on mid-run failure emits a `partial_results` JSON event to stderr listing every batch attempted before returning the classified error.

patches.summary: Guard `syncDependentResource` against path templates that declare placeholders beyond `{ParentIDParam}`. Skips the dependent with a structured `sync_warning` (mirroring the existing `syncResource` hierarchical-API guard) instead of firing HTTP requests with literal `{tableIdOrName}`/`{recordId}`/`{webhookId}` segments.
patches.reason: Airtable's records / comments / webhook-payloads dependents each require multi-level enumeration (tables-per-base, records-per-table, webhook-IDs-per-base) the current sync loop does not perform. Without this guard the dependent pass silently produced zero rows and 404s on every parent; Greptile P1 review (PR #829) called this out. The guard keeps `sync` honest while leaving room for a future enumeration walker to fill those placeholders properly.
patches.validated_outcome: `go build`, `go vet`, and `go test ./...` all pass; the dependent loop emits a `sync_warning` with `reason=dependent_path_unresolved` listing the unresolved keys instead of issuing the bad request.

patches.summary: Scope `traverse` lookups to the user-supplied baseID by adding `AND parent_id = ?` to the per-frontier `SELECT data FROM records WHERE id = ?` query.
patches.reason: Greptile P1 (PR #829, round 2) flagged that the original code explicitly discarded the baseID argument via `_ = baseID`, so multi-base mirrors could return edges from unrelated bases that happened to share a `rec...` prefix. parent_id is populated by dependent sync with the parent baseID, so adding it to the WHERE clause is the minimal correct scope.
patches.validated_outcome: `go build`, `go vet`, and `go test ./...` all pass; the traversal frontier now only walks records whose `parent_id` matches the user-supplied baseID.

patches.summary: Scope `history record` payload scans by joining the raw payload rows in `resources` (resource_type='webhooks') against the dedicated `webhooks` subscription table on `id`, restricting to subscriptions whose `parent_id` matches the user-supplied baseID. LEFT JOIN with an IS NULL fallback preserves legacy mirrors that pre-date the dedicated webhooks table.
patches.reason: Greptile P1 (PR #829, round 2) flagged that the original SELECT used only `WHERE resource_type='webhooks'` with no base scoping, so multi-base mirrors mixed payload events from every base whose webhook IDs accidentally collided in the local cache. Airtable webhook payloads don't carry baseId at the top level, so the correct scope is the webhook-subscription join.
patches.validated_outcome: `go build`, `go vet`, and `go test ./...` all pass; the payload scan now joins through the dedicated webhooks subscription table and filters by `parent_id = baseID OR parent_id IS NULL` (the IS NULL branch keeps legacy mirrors functional).

patches.summary: Scope `stale` record lookups by passing baseID (not tableID) into the `parent_id = ?` predicate. tableID is still consumed by the field/equals filter and the user-facing message.
patches.reason: Greptile P1 (PR #829, round 3) caught the same wrong-scope pattern in stale.go that earlier rounds patched in traverse.go and history_record.go: the original code threaded tableID into the parent_id filter, which never matches a real row (parent_id is populated by dependent sync with the parent baseID).
patches.validated_outcome: `go build`, `go vet`, and `go test -count=1 ./internal/cli/... ./internal/store/...` all pass; stale lookups now filter rows whose `parent_id = baseID` (or IS NULL for legacy mirrors).

patches.summary: Make `webhooks fleet --all-profiles` actually iterate profile databases. Builds a dedup'd list of (profile-name, db-path) targets from `loadProfileStore().Profiles[*].Values["db"]`, opens each read-only, and aggregates results tagged with `profile`/`db_path` so multi-tenant operators can see which mirror each webhook came from. Missing/unopenable per-profile mirrors warn to stderr and are skipped, not fatal.
patches.reason: Greptile P1 (PR #829, round 3) flagged that the original `--all-profiles` flag's only code path was the early-return under `IsVerifyEnv()` — in every real invocation it was a silent no-op, despite documentation claiming multi-tenant scanning. This patch makes the flag actually do what the docs and Help text promise.
patches.validated_outcome: `go build`, `go vet`, and `go test -count=1 ./internal/cli/... ./internal/store/...` all pass; `--all-profiles` now enumerates configured profiles, dedupes by db-path, and aggregates webhook rows across each opened mirror. Default (no --all-profiles) behavior is unchanged.
